architectural_units.name: Leader
architectural_units.description: This microservice has as its main function the routing of all communications to the corresponding microservice within the system architecture.

architectural_units.name: Portal
architectural_units.description: The portal microservice has as its main function to offer a centralized interface for access to the different VWGS applications.

architectural_units.name: Access Control
architectural_units.description: The Access Control microservice has as its main objective the management of user authentication and their permissions within the application.

architectural_units.name: Communication Log
architectural_units.description: The Communication Log microservice has as its main purpose to register all communications that occur within the system, both between microservices and with external services.

architectural_units.name: Scheduler
architectural_units.description: This microservice has as its main function the planning and programming of processes within the system.

architectural_units.name: Angular
architectural_units.description: Angular is a web development framework created by Google, based on the programming language superset of JavaScript called TypeScript, which allows building modern single-page web applications (SPA).

architectural_units.name: Spring Boot
architectural_units.description: Spring Boot is a framework that simplifies the creation of Java applications based on Spring, offering automatic configuration and tools that allow deploying applications quickly.

architectural_units.name: Amazon Web Services
architectural_units.description: The provider for this project is Amazon Web Services which has a wide catalog of cloud services and resources.

architectural_units.name: Kubernetes
architectural_units.description: Kubernetes (K8s), a container orchestration platform created by Google.

architectural_units.name: Docker
architectural_units.description: The deployment process for our application begins with the creation of a Docker image for each microservice.

architectural_units.name: Presentation Layer
architectural_units.description: The presentation layer receives requests and builds responses.

architectural_units.name: Business Logic Layer
architectural_units.description: The business logic layer applies the domain rules.

architectural_units.name: Data Access Layer
architectural_units.description: The data access layer interacts with the database.

architectural_units.name: Domain Layer
architectural_units.description: The domain layer defines the data model.
The Leader microservice has as its main function the routing of all communications to the corresponding microservice within the system architecture.

The portal microservice has as its main function to offer a centralized interface for access to the different VWGS applications. [...] The portal microservice incorporates the binaries necessary for the frontEnd both of the portal itself and of the rest of the portal applications.

The client, which we also call frontEnd, is responsible for the presentation and user experience of the application, encapsulating the interface logic and the coordination of calls to the server's API.
The data access layer interacts with the database.

architectural_units.name: REST
architectural_units.description: The access to data and the management of logic in this project is carried out through REST operations, which structure and normalize communication with the data layer.

architectural_units.name: HTTP
architectural_units.description: The message exchange protocol used in this case is HTTP.

architectural_units.name: JSON
architectural_units.description: The data format used is JSON.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The application has an architecture based on microservices. It consists of dividing the system into a set of small, independent and autonomous services where each microservice is responsible for a specific functionality.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application is designed, deployed and executed using cloud services (cloud computing) instead of local or physical servers.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application follows the Client-Server pattern which organizes the code into two differentiated components: the client, which formulates service requests, and the server, which receives, processes and returns responses.

patterns.name: MVVM
patterns.description: Angular applies the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) pattern, since its architecture is based on components and services.

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: Spring Boot organizes the code following the layered pattern with which responsibilities are separated.
